candidate.name: SPDP Repair Lemma 1
candidate.statement: There exists a polynomial function f: R -> d such that for any labelled SPDP profile P, if the row span of P is not full dimensional, then there exists an f(P) which can repair this gap by adding at most (f(P))^2 new rows.
proof_sketch: Construct a finite set of polynomial functions that can repair the span gap for each SPDP profile.
Show that for any profile, f(P) ≤ (dim(R))^2, where dim(R) is the number of labelled interfaces.
Use algebraic invariants to prove that the added rows indeed repair the span gap without requiring SAT hardness.

candidate.name: SPDP Repair Lemma 2
candidate.statement: For any given SPDP profile P with row span deficiency, there exists a finite set of polynomial functions S such that adding one function from S to each deficient row in P results in an SPDP profile with full-dimensional row span.
proof_sketch: Construct a finite set of polynomial functions that can repair the row span deficiency for each deficient SPDP profile.
Show that applying any function from S to a deficient row increases its dimension without requiring SAT hardness or exceeding polynomial bounds.
Prove through algebraic means that this process results in a full-dimensional row span.

candidate.name: SPDP Repair Lemma 3
candidate.statement: For any given SPDP profile P with an orbit span deficiency, there exists a finite set of polynomial functions T such that applying each function from T to every row in P results in an SPDP profile with no orbit span deficiencies.
proof_sketch: Construct a finite set of polynomial functions that can repair the orbit span deficiency for each deficient SPDP profile.
Show that applying any function from T to a row decreases its orbit size without requiring SAT hardness or exceeding polynomial bounds.
Prove through algebraic means that this process results in an SPDP profile with no orbit span deficiencies.
